training_lineage_contract: walkcurr rl_only (tracks.json): both composed policies are independently-trained clean-RL checkpoints already covered by bundle_rlonly_stance_v1 (rise+hold, s5-klrollback05-acq15m) and bundle_rlonly_v2 (forward walk, crutchoff-s0-warmadapt-acq1) -- see those manifests for each role's own lineage contract. This manifest adds NO new training and NO new weights: it is a RUNTIME composition (which policy is live + which of that policy's own already-trained motor/safety contract is active) driven purely by role-selection/config-selection plumbing -- explicitly allowed as non-motion plumbing under RL_GOALS.md's rl_only clarification. No scripted joint trajectory, teacher target, or demonstration enters this composition at any point: at the handoff tick the walk policy is simply handed the stance role's own exact physical state (qpos/qvel/ctrl/act + the safety layer's slew memory) and takes over immediately.

composition_mechanism.description: Two SimHexapodJointWalkEnv instances, one per role's own exact recorded cfg-set (stance: probe_currentcap29_flatonly.BASE_CFG_ARGS+FLATONLY_OVERRIDE_ARGS; walk: cfg_recipe_walk50hz_rlonly_v2.CFG_ARGS -- each role's real bus.write_speed/write_acc, safety.max_delta_q_deg, goal.joint_action_bias_* differ and are cached at env construction, so cannot hot-swap on one live env). At the handoff tick the stance role's raw physical state (qpos, qvel, ctrl, act, safety._last_safe) is copied from the rise env into a freshly-reset walk env (fresh plant-frame goal/tilt/height anchors, same 'reanchor_keep_state' trick eval_handoff.py already established), then mj_forward + a rebuilt observation. No joint trajectory is scripted between the two; only the live policy and its config envelope change.
composition_mechanism.why_two_envs_is_still_a_fair_test: qpos/qvel are physical generalized coordinates of the SAME MJCF model (env.model_source=mesh_mjx both sides) -- identical layout regardless of which role's cfg built the env -- so the copy is a like-for-like physical continuation, not a teleport.
